extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and patentees preparing or examining reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on oath/declaration, supplemental declarations, who may sign, fee requirements, maintenance fee treatment, surrender of original patent, and related procedural requirements for U.S. reissue patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign the reissue declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration must be executed by or with respect to each inventor before the case can be released for examination. The assignee of 100% of the entire right, title and interest (who must be named as the reissue applicant) may sign the declaration if the application does not seek to enlarge the scope of the claims in the original patent, or the original application was filed under 37 CFR 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue applicant is a juristic entity, the declaration must be signed by an official who has a title that carries apparent authority or by someone who makes a statement of authorization to act (e.g., employee authorized by corporate resolution). A patent practitioner may sign the reissue declaration as an official of a juristic entity only if given authority as explained above and may not sign a substitute statement merely on the basis of having power of attorney. See MPEP § 605.01 and 37 CFR 1.175(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement for unavailable inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee, or current patent owner if there has been an assignment, may sign a substitute statement in accordance with 37 CFR 1.64 on behalf of an inventor who is deceased, legally incapacitated, cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, or refused to execute the oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substitute-statement procedure is available even if the reissue application was filed to enlarge claim scope (e.g., a broadening reissue), pursuant to 37 CFR 1.175(c) and § 1.64. Forms such as PTO/AIA/07 may be used where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms available for reissue declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the circumstances, form PTO/AIA/05 (Reissue Application Declaration By The Inventor), PTO/AIA/06 (Reissue Application Declaration By The Assignee), or PTO/AIA/07 (Substitute Statement in Lieu of an Oath or Declaration for Reissue Patent Application) may be used to prepare a declaration in a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-September 16, 2012 filings alternative forms PTO/SB/51 or PTO/SB/52 may be used. Use the form appropriate to filing date and circumstances; see MPEP references in the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175 substantive requirements for reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012 the reissue oath/declaration, in addition to complying with § 1.63, must state: (1) the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of claiming more or less than the patentee had the right to claim, stating at least one error being relied upon as the basis for reissue; and (2) all errors being corrected in the reissue application up to the time of filing arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any error corrected that is not covered by the original oath/declaration requires a supplemental oath/declaration. The examiner checks for presence of the averment, not the truth of absence of deceptive intent. See pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175 and MPEP § 1414.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration requirement (pre-AIA filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-September 16, 2012 reissue applications, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration is required where additional errors (not covered by a previously submitted oath/declaration) are corrected, unless they are only spelling, grammar, typographical, editorial or clerical errors not considered errors under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental declaration must state that every such error arose without any deceptive intention. It must be submitted before allowance and may be submitted with any amendment prior to allowance or to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 251 rejection. Example language is provided in the MPEP. Use Form PTO/SB/51S where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration not required (post-AIA filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, if additional defects or errors are corrected after filing the reissue oath/declaration, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where all previously identified errors are no longer being relied upon as the basis for reissue, the applicant must explicitly identify on the record an error being relied upon to support reissue; the identification must be conspicuous and comply with 35 U.S.C. 251 (see 37 CFR 1.175(d)). See MPEP § 1414.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required by 37 CFR 1.63 in reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration must comply with pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 and include the averments required by 1.63(a) and (b): (A) that applicants have reviewed and understand the contents of the specification, including claims as amended; (B) believe the named inventor(s) to be the original and first inventor(s) of the claimed subject matter; and (C) acknowledge the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to be material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP should review reissue oaths/declarations for compliance with 1.63; the examiner is not required to do so. See MPEP § 602 and MPEP § 1414.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: When supplemental oath/declaration must specifically identify an error
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reissue oath/declaration must specifically identify an error being relied upon to support reissue only where: (A) the prior reissue oath/declaration failed to state an error; (B) the prior oath/declaration attempted but did not properly state an error; or (C) all errors under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 251 stated in prior oath(s)/declaration(s) are no longer being corrected in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error was previously and properly stated and is still being corrected, there is no need to specifically identify additional errors; the examiner should not review any voluntarily-stated further errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: supplemental oath/declaration must be submitted before allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental reissue oath/declaration required by pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) must be submitted before allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to correct an error after allowance of the reissue application, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration must accompany the requested correction stating the errors arose without deceptive intention. See MPEP § 1444 for examiner action to obtain the supplemental oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration in broadening reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadening reissue application must be applied for by all of the inventors; the original reissue oath/declaration must be signed by all inventors. If a supplemental oath/declaration is subsequently needed in a broadening reissue to fulfill pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175 requirements, it must be signed by all inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor refuses or cannot be found to sign, a supplemental declaration listing all inventors and signed by all available inventors may be filed if accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with fee requesting waiver of the nonsigning inventor’s signature. If a sole inventor refuses or cannot be found, a supplemental declaration signed by the assignee or a party showing sufficient proprietary interest may be filed with a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic reissue application filing, search, and examination fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications the following fees are required: basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(e)), search fee (37 CFR 1.16(n)), examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(r)), application size fee if applicable (37 CFR 1.16(s)), and excess claims fees if applicable (37 CFR 1.16(h) and (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic filing, search and examination fees are due on filing but may be paid later within the time set in 37 CFR 1.53(f) with applicable surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)). Use Reissue Application Fee Transmittal Forms PTO/AIA/50 (for filings on/after Sept 16, 2012) or PTO/SB/56 (before that date). See MPEP § 1415.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee calculation and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: An application size fee applies where the specification and drawings exceed 100 sheets of paper; the fee applies for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof over 100 sheets (37 CFR 1.16(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calculation of number of sheets excludes any Sequence Listing, computer readable form (CRF) of a Sequence Listing, Computer Program Listing Appendix filed as ASCII plain text, or Sequence Listing XML filed in XML via approved methods (see 37 CFR 1.52(f), 1.821(c)/(e), 1.831(a), 1.96(c)). See MPEP § 607.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees apply per 37 CFR 1.16(h) for each independent claim in excess of three and per 37 CFR 1.16(i) for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications filed on/after Dec 8, 2004, where a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) to expressly abandon was filed on/after Mar 10, 2006, applicant may request refund of search and excess claims fees paid in the application (see MPEP § 711.01). The number of claims in the original patent is not relevant in determining excess claims fees for a reissue. Excess claims fees due with an amendment are required before any consideration of the amendment by the examiner; additions of claims require payment. Amendments filed before first Office action presenting additional claims without full fees will not be entered and will be non-responsive (see MPEP § 714.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation basis for excess claims fees with amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional fees due with an amendment are calculated on the basis of the claims (total and independent) which would be present if the amendment were entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment only revises existing claims and does not add new claims, no excess claim fee is required. Cancellation of claims in a preliminary amendment can reduce fees to be paid; however, no refund will be made for claims canceled after fees were already paid. Where excess claims fees have previously been paid, a later amendment affecting the claims cannot serve as the basis for granting any refund (37 CFR 1.26(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee for reissue patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue fee for issuing each reissue patent is set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure payment per the rule when preparing for reissue patent issuance. See MPEP § 1415.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees do not change schedule by filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a reissue application does not alter the schedule of payments of maintenance fees on the original patent. If maintenance fees have not been paid on the original patent as required and the patent has expired, no reissue patent can be granted because 35 U.S.C. 251 only authorizes granting a reissue for the unexpired term of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should determine whether all required maintenance fees have been paid before conducting examination and again prior to issuing any Office action or preparing reissue for issue. Use the Patent Maintenance Fees Storefront, Fee Payment History Service, or Docket Application Viewer (DAV) to confirm payment. Contact OPLA if the maintenance fee window has closed and fee unpaid. See MPEP § 1415.01 and Chapter 2500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of maintenance fees when reissue patent involved
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original patent required maintenance fees, the schedule of payments on the original patent continues for the reissue patent (37 CFR 1.362(h)). If a maintenance fee is due prior to issuance of a reissue patent, the maintenance fee must be paid in the original patent to maintain the reissue patent in force beyond the grace period and to maintain pendency of any reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue application scheduled to issue is the only or last pending reissue application, payment should be made in the original patent at least a day prior to issue date to avoid uncertainty. If not paid before issue, payment during the grace period must include the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.20(h). Design and plant patents do not require maintenance fees (37 CFR 1.362(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee treatment when multiple reissue patents exist (post-Jan 16, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Jan 16, 2018, separate maintenance fee payments are required for each utility reissue patent during the unexpired part of the term of the original patent (unless the original was filed before Dec 12, 1980).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously a single maintenance fee for multiple reissued patents was sometimes sufficient; that practice was discontinued. If more than one reissue patent replaces the original, maintenance fees must be paid in each reissue patent. If one or more reissue applications are pending on the maintenance fee due date, maintenance fees are still required in the original patent that is not surrendered. See MPEP § 2504 and § 1415.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: No physical surrender of original patent required
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for reissue constitutes an offer to surrender the original patent, and surrender takes effect upon the grant of the reissue patent; physical surrender of the letters patent is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to Oct 21, 2004 physical surrender was required. If the patentee submitted the original letters patent in the reissue application, the Office may return it in response to a timely request when it can be readily retrieved. Requests to return after payment of the issue fee require a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b). If the original letters patent cannot be located, the Office will not create a new one. See MPEP § 1416 and 37 CFR 1.178(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools to determine maintenance fee payment history
rubrics_metrics.description: The history of maintenance fees is determined through the Patent Maintenance Fees Storefront, Fee Payment History Service, or Docket Application Viewer (DAV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one tool does not show payment, examiners should confirm through the others. Links: https://fees.uspto.gov/MaintenanceFees/ and https://feeprocessingportal.uspto.gov/fpng/fees/historyservice. From DAV open the patented file and view 'Application Data' tab. If fee window closed and unpaid, contact OPLA for instructions.
